Synthesis and electromagnetic characterization of frequency selective 1 radar absorbing materials using carbon nanopowders 2 3 Davide Micheli*1, Antonio Vricella, Roberto Pastore, Mario Marchetti 4 Astronautic, Electric and Energy Engineering Department, 5 Sapienza University of Rome, Via Salaria 851, 00138 Rome, Italy 6 Abstract 7 A new method for the synthesis of multilayered radar absorbing materials is analyzed by using 8 carbon nanomaterials
With respect to the literature, a desired profile of reflection coefficient is a 9 priori established as a function of the frequency

The goal of the synthesis is to follow this target 10 profile by computing thickness and type of the material of each layer until the reflection 11 coefficient of the electromagnetic-wave absorber best approximates the wanted reflection 12 coefficient

The material available for each layer is epoxy-resin reinforced by different kind of 13 carbon-based nano/micro powders: graphene nanoplatelets, carbon nanofibers, multi-walled 14 carbon nanotubes and polyaniline
The dielectric characterization of the composite materials is 15 performed in the frequency range 2÷18 GHz
The synthesis uses evolutionary computation by 16 drawing on the electric permittivity of composite materials
Three square layered electromagnetic 17 wave absorbers of 25 cm side are manufactured

The comparison between the target, the simulated 18 and the measured reflection coefficients shows a good agreement thus confirming the scientific 19 validity of the dielectric characterization and the proposed design method
Finally, a finite element 20 analysis has been carried out to explain the mechanism of electromagnetic wave absorption by a 21 multilayer and to simulate a low radar observable naval military gun
